74: ## 3. CSV Export Specification (RFC 4180)
75: 
76: ### 3.1 Framing, Line Breaks & Encoding
77: - **MIME Type**: `text/csv; charset=utf-8`
78: - **Line Delimiter**: Strict CRLF (`\r\n`, ASCII `0x0D 0x0A`) per RFC 4180 § 2.1.
79: - **Field Delimiter**: ASCII comma (`,`, `0x2C`).
80: - **Header Line**: The first record in the exported file MUST be the column header list, matching the exact order of data columns.
81: - **Field Quoting**: Any field containing a comma, double-quote, or newline must be enclosed within double-quotes (`"..."`). An embedded double-quote character must be escaped with an adjacent double-quote (`""`) per RFC 4180 § 2.7.
82: - **Numeric Formatting**: Invariant culture (`CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`). Decimal separator MUST be period (`.`); thousands separators are strictly forbidden.
83: - **Byte Order Mark (BOM)**: Optional UTF-8 BOM (`0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF`) may be enabled for Microsoft Excel compatibility, but plain UTF-8 is the default.
84: 
85: ### 3.2 Time Synchronization & Precision Standards
86: DJI flight logs contain multiple asynchronous clocks (mobile device system time, flight controller ticks, GPS epochs). The CSV exporter synchronizes these into four canonical time columns:
87: 
88: 1. **`DateTime(UTC)`**: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`) derived from the log details start milliseconds plus relative record offset.
89: 2. **`DateTime(Local)`**: Localized ISO 8601 timestamp with explicit UTC offset (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sss+HH:MM`).
90: 3. **`Time(millisecond)`**: Cumulative elapsed milliseconds since flight logging initiated ($t \ge 0$). Monotonically increasing.
91: 4. **`OSD.flyTime [s]`**: Airborne flight controller timer in seconds (scaled deci-seconds $\div 10.0$). Begins at $0.0$ when propulsion motors spin up.
92: 
93: ### 3.3 Geodetic Coordinate & Vertical Altitude Standards
94: 1. **Horizontal Coordinates**:
95:    - `OSD.latitude [deg]` & `OSD.longitude [deg]`: Signed decimal degrees (WGS84).
96:    - Coordinate Precision: Formatted with **8 decimal places** (`{:.8}`), corresponding to $\approx 1.1\text{ mm}$ spatial resolution at the equator.
97: 2. **Vertical Datums**:
98:    - `OSD.height [m]`: Relative takeoff altitude above ground level (AGL) in meters, derived from barometric altimeter ($0.1\text{ m}$ resolution).
99:    - `OSD.altitude_msl [m]`: Orthometric height above Mean Sea Level ($H$) derived by adjusting GPS/RTK ellipsoidal height ($h$) with the local EGM2008 geoid undulation ($N$):
100:      $$H = h - N(\phi, \lambda)$$
101:    - `VPS.height [m]`: Downward-facing ultrasonic / optical flow ground clearance ($0.0 \dots 10.0\text{ m}$).

222: ### 4.3 3D Flight Path Geometry (`<LineString>`) & Coordinate Tuples
223: 1. **Coordinate Tuple Order**:
224:    In KML, coordinates are defined strictly as:
225:    $$\text{longitude},\text{latitude},\text{altitude}$$
226:    > ⚠️ **Critical Rule**: Longitude ($-180.0 \dots +180.0$) MUST precede Latitude ($-90.0 \dots +90.0$). Reversing this order places the drone trajectory on the opposite hemisphere.
227: 2. **Tuple Delimiters**:
228:    - Internal tuple components are separated by commas (`,`) without whitespace: `lon,lat,alt`.
229:    - Distinct coordinates along the path are separated by newline or single space:
230:      ```xml
231:      <coordinates>
232:        -122.33214500,47.60621200,142.50
233:        -122.33215600,47.60623400,143.10
234:        -122.33217800,47.60626700,144.20
235:      </coordinates>
236:      ```

238: ### 4.4 Altitude Modes & Vertical Extrusion
239: - **Airborne Flight Path**:
240:   ```xml
241:   <LineString>
242:     <extrude>1</extrude>
243:     <altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>
244:     <coordinates>...</coordinates>
245:   </LineString>
246:   ```
247:   - `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`: Treats coordinates as absolute Mean Sea Level (MSL) altitude in meters ($H = h - N$). In Google Earth, this ensures the trajectory is positioned at its real-world physical elevation above sea level.
248:   - `<extrude>1</extrude>`: Drops a semi-transparent curtain from the airborne polyline directly down to the ground terrain surface. The curtain color is governed by the `<PolyStyle>` defined in the active `<Style>`.
249: - **2D Ground Track (Shadow)**:
250:   ```xml
251:   <Placemark>
252:     <name>Ground Track</name>
253:     <styleUrl>#LineStyleGroundTrack</styleUrl>
254:     <LineString>
255:       <altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>
256:       <coordinates>...</coordinates>
257:     </LineString>
258:   </Placemark>
259:   ```
260:   `<altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>` projects the flight footprint directly onto Google Earth's digital terrain model, providing an unobstructed horizontal path view.
261: 
262: ### 4.5 Color Encoding Model (`aabbggrr`) & Speed/Altitude Segment Styling
263: KML encodes 32-bit colors in **hexadecimal ABGR order** (`aabbggrr`):
264: $$\text{Color}_{\text{KML}} = \text{Alpha (2 hex)} + \text{Blue (2 hex)} + \text{Green (2 hex)} + \text{Red (2 hex)}$$
265: 
266: #### Mathematical Conversion from Web Hex `#RRGGBB` with Transparency $T \in [0, 100]\%$:
267: 1. Opacity percentage: $\alpha = 100 - T$
268: 2. Hex Alpha: $AA = \text{format!("{:02x}", \lfloor \alpha \times 2.55 \rfloor)}$
269: 3. Given `#RRGGBB`, extract $RR = \text{hex}[0..2]$, $GG = \text{hex}[2..4]$, $BB = \text{hex}[4..6]$:
270:    $$\text{KmlColor} = AA + BB + GG + RR$$
271: 
272: #### Segmented Trajectory Transitions:
273: When the flight state transitions (e.g. from Normal flight to a High Wind Warning or Low Battery Failsafe), the exporter closes the current `<Placemark>` and opens a new `<Placemark>` with the corresponding style:
274: - Normal cruise $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleNormal</styleUrl>`
275: - Non-critical warning $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleWarning</styleUrl>`

341: ### 4.7 3D Trajectory Decimation & Simplification (RDP Algorithm)
342: Extracted from `KmlCompressor.cs` in the decompiled codebase, raw 10 Hz flight paths contain substantial GPS hover jitter that inflates file size and causes rendering lag in Google Earth. OpenFlightReader implements a multi-stage 3D path reduction pipeline:
343: 1. **Jitter Filter**: Coincident or near-static points where 3D displacement $\Delta d < 0.15\text{ m}$ (`jitterMeters = 0.15`) are collapsed.
344: 2. **3D Projection to Local Metric Frame**: Coordinates are transformed from spherical degrees to local metric offsets with vertical scaling (`altitudeScale = 1.6`) to preserve vertical profiles.
345: 3. **Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) 3D**: Applies recursive RDP line simplification with default perpendicular tolerance $\epsilon = 0.45\text{ m}$ (`tolerance = 0.45`).
346: 4. **Collinear Point Cleanup**: Eliminates redundant intermediate vertices along straight flight lines with angular deviation $< 0.08\text{ rad}$.

590: ## 7. Filtering & Decimation Specification
591: 
592: ### 7.1 Time Window Filtering (`--start`, `--end`)
593: The CLI and export pipeline support flexible temporal windowing:
594: - **Command-line flags**:
595:   - `--start <START>`: Begins export at specified time.
596:   - `--end <END>`: Terminates export at specified time.
597: - **Allowed Formats**:
598:   1. **Floating-point seconds from start**: e.g., `--start 30.5 --end 120.0` (sclices $30.5\text{ s} \le t_{\text{elapsed}} \le 120.0\text{ s}$).
599:   2. **ISO 8601 UTC timestamp**: e.g., `--start 2026-10-27T14:33:00Z`.
600:   3. **Standard colon time**: e.g., `--start 01:30 --end 05:45` ($MM:SS$).
601: - **Boundary Validation**:
602:   - Requires $t_{\text{start}} < t_{\text{end}}$.
603:   - If $t_{\text{start}} \ge \text{Duration}$, export yields an empty sequence and emits a warning.
604:   - If $t_{\text{end}} > \text{Duration}$, clamping to EOF occurs without error.
605:   - Slicing semantics: Half-open interval $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}})$ or inclusive $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$.
606: 
607: ### 7.2 Frequency & Stride Decimation (`--rate`, `--step`)
608: High-frequency blackbox streams (.DAT: 50–200 Hz) and mobile logs (.txt: 10 Hz) often generate too much data for lightweight web viewers or spreadsheet editors.
609: - **`--rate <HZ>`**: Sets maximum output frequency in Hertz (Hz):
610:   - `--rate 1`: Exactly 1 record per second ($1.0\text{ Hz}$).
611:   - `--rate 5`: 5 records per second ($5.0\text{ Hz}$).
612:   - `--rate 0.5`: 1 record every 2 seconds ($0.5\text{ Hz}$).
613: - **`--step <N>`**: Stride decimation exporting every $N$-th record ($N \ge 1$).
614: 
615: #### Uniform Time-Binning Algorithm:
616: Given target sample rate $R\text{ Hz}$ with bin duration $\Delta t = \frac{1.0}{R}\text{ seconds}$:
617: 1. Divide the time axis into intervals $I_k = [k \Delta t, (k+1) \Delta t)$.
618: 2. For each interval $I_k$, select the record whose timestamp $t_i$ minimizes the absolute error $|t_i - (k + 0.5)\Delta t|$.
619: 3. Guarantees uniform time spacing without time drift.
620: 
621: ### 7.3 Critical Landmark Pinning & Event Preservation
622: Decimation must NEVER eliminate mission-critical single-frame events. The decimator marks the following records as **pinned** so they survive decimation:
623: 1. **Takeoff Event**: First record where `OSD.isMotorUp == 1` and `OSD.flyTime > 0`.
624: 2. **Home Point Calibration**: The record where `HOME.isHomeRecord == true` is first registered or updated.
625: 3. **Flight Mode Transitions**: Records where `OSD.flightMode` changes state (e.g. `P-GPS` $\to$ `Sport` or `Manual` $\to$ `Auto-RTH`).
626: 4. **Safety Alerts & Warnings**: Any record with a non-empty `APP.warning` or `ShowSeriousWarning`.
627: 5. **RTH Failsafe Activations**: Record where `GoHomeStatus` transitions to active.
628: 6. **Max Altitude / Max Speed Extremum**: Points where maximum altitude or speed is achieved.
629: 7. **Touchdown / Landing Event**: Final record where motors disarm (`OSD.isMotorUp == 0`).
630: 
631: ### 7.4 Downsampling Algorithms (RDP & LTTB)
632: - **Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) 3D**: Used for spatial vector reduction in KML and GeoJSON. Recursively finds the point of maximum perpendicular distance from the line segment connecting endpoints; if distance exceeds tolerance $\epsilon$ ($0.45\text{ m}$), the point is preserved.
633: - **Largest Triangle Three Buckets (LTTB)**: Used for numeric time-series downsampling (altitude profiles, battery cell curves, velocity charts) in web dashboards. Downsamples 100,000 points down to 1,000–2,000 points while preserving peaks, valleys, and visual waveform fidelity.

411: ## 5. Streaming Record Envelope Iterators
412: 
413: `flightreader-core` provides two zero-allocation stream iterators for processing raw binary files without loading millions of decoded structures into memory simultaneously.
414: 
415: ### 5.1 `.txt` Record Envelope Iterator (`RecordEnvelopeIterator<'a>`)
416: 
417: Located in `crates/flightreader-core/src/txt/record.rs`.
418: 
419: #### Stream Wire Framing
420: Every `.txt` telemetry envelope adheres to the wire format:
421: ```
422: +---------------+-----------------------------+--------------------+-----------------------+
423: | Record Type   | Length (L)                  | Payload Data       | Delimiter Sentinel    |
424: | uint8 (1B)    | uint8 (1B, v1-6) or         | uint8[L]           | 0xFF / 255 (1B)       |
425: |               | uint16_le (2B, v7-14)       |                    |                       |
426: +---------------+-----------------------------+--------------------+-----------------------+
427: ```
428: 
429: #### Initialization & Boundary Partitioning
430: ```rust
431: pub fn new(buffer: &'a [u8], header: &TxtHeader) -> Result<Self>;
432: ```
433: - **Stream Boundaries**:
434:   - For `v1..=11` (`DetailsLocation::EndOfFile`): Telemetry envelopes start at `header.header_length` (100) and terminate at `header.details_offset`.
435:   - For `v12..=14` (`DetailsLocation::HeaderOffset`): Telemetry envelopes begin at `header.details_offset` and run through to `buffer.len()`.
436: - **Resilient Resynchronization (`with_resync(true)`)**: Default mode. Corrupted delimiter bytes or truncated records do not abort iteration; the cursor scans forward byte-by-byte (`cursor += 1`) to re-acquire the next valid `[type, length, payload, 0xFF]` envelope.
437: 
438: #### Payload De-Scrambling & Decryption Routing
439: Iteration yields `Result<RawRecordEnvelope<'a>, FlightReaderError>`. The caller then decodes the payload:
440: - **`env.decode_payload(version: u8) -> Result<RecordPayload<'a>>`**:
441:   - `v1..=6`: Returns `RecordPayload::Borrowed(&'a [u8])` with zero heap allocation.
442:   - `v7..=12`: Automatically applies ECMA-182 CRC64 cyclic XOR de-scrambling; returns `RecordPayload::Owned(Vec<u8>)`.
443:   - `v13..=14`:
444:     - FeaturePoint 8 plaintext bypass (Type 50 `FlightRecordRecover`, Type 56 `KeyStorage`): Unscrambled directly.
445:     - Encrypted records: If configured with an `AesContinuousIvEngine`, decrypts in-place with continuous IV chaining; if unconfigured, returns intermediate ciphertext.
446: - **`iter.decode_into(&env, out_buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<&[u8]>`**: Zero-heap in-place decoding into a caller-provided reusable scratch slice.
447:

450: ### 5.2 `.DAT` Blackbox Frame Iterator (`DatFrameIterator<'a>`)
451: 
452: Located in `crates/flightreader-core/src/dat/frame.rs`.
453: 
454: #### Stream Wire Framing
455: Every `.DAT` blackbox frame adheres to the 9-byte header framing:
456: ```
457: +------------+------------+---------------+---------------+--------------------+--------------------------------+---------------+
458: | Magic Byte | Frame Len  | Sequence Byte | Payload ID    | Timestamp (Ticks)  | Raw Payload                    | Checksum      |
459: | 0x55 (1B)  | uint8 (1B) | uint8 (1B)    | uint16_le(2B) | uint32_le (4B)     | uint8[Len - 9 - ChecksumLen]   | CRC16 / CRC32 |
460: +------------+------------+---------------+---------------+--------------------+--------------------------------+---------------+
461: ```
462: 
463: #### Iterator Operation
464: ```rust
465: let mut iter = DatFrameIterator::new(&dat_bytes);
466: while let Some(frame_res) = iter.next() {
467:     let frame = frame_res?;
468:     // frame.payload_id: u16
469:     // frame.timestamp_ticks: u32 (microseconds since boot)
470:     // frame.payload: &'a [u8]
471:     let decoded = parse_dat_payload(frame.payload_id, frame.payload)?;
472: }
473: ```
474: - **Synchronization**: Searches for magic byte `0x55`.
475: - **Integrity Validation**: Evaluates CRC16-CCITT (`0x1021` polynomial, testing primary seed `0x3692` and fallback `0xFFFF`), or CRC32 (`0xEDB88320`) for frames $\ge 13$ bytes.
476: - **Recovery**: Invalid candidate lengths ($< 11$) or checksum mismatches advance the search cursor by 1 byte, seamlessly ignoring noise or corrupted sectors.

480: ## 6. Timestamp Handling & Time Synchronization
481: 
482: A critical responsibility of `flightreader-export` is constructing deterministic, monotonic time-series timestamps for tabular (CSV) and GIS (KML, GPX, GeoJSON) representations.
483: 
484: ### 6.1 `.txt` Mobile Telemetry Timestamps
485: 
486: In DJI `.txt` logs, timestamps are derived from two distinct locations:
487: 
488: 1. **Base Session Start Timestamp (`DetailsLogStartMilliseconds`)**:
489:    - Location: Inside the Details / Summary block (at `header.details_offset`).
490:    - Format: 64-bit Little-Endian signed integer (`int64`), representing UTC Unix Epoch in milliseconds ($t_0$).
491: 2. **Cumulative Sortie Flight Time (`OsdRecord.fly_time_s`)**:
492:    - Location: Bytes 42..44 of OSD Record Type 1 (`LittleEndian::read_u16(&payload[42..44]) as f64 / 10.0`).
493:    - Format: Elapsed motor running duration in seconds with 0.1s resolution ($t_{\text{rel}}$).
494: 3. **Synthesis & Reconstruction**:
495:    - For post-takeoff samples ($t_{\text{rel}} > 0$):
496:      $$\text{EpochMs}(i) = \text{DetailsLogStartMilliseconds} + \left( \text{fly\_time\_s}(i) \times 1000.0 \right)$$
497:    - For pre-takeoff ground records ($t_{\text{rel}} == 0.0$):
498:      Since the drone is stationary prior to motor arming, consecutive OSD records arrive at nominal 10 Hz cadence (100 ms intervals). An incremental counter $\Delta t_{\text{ground}} = k \times 100\text{ ms}$ should be applied to prevent all ground points from collapsing into identical timestamps.
499:    - If `DetailsLogStartMilliseconds` is zero or the Details block is truncated:
500:      The exporter must fallback to relative elapsed time from flight inception ($t = 0.000\text{ s}$).
501: 
502: ### 6.2 `.DAT` Blackbox Timestamps
503: 
504: In `.DAT` files, every frame header provides an exact hardware clock counter:
505: - Field: `DatFrame.timestamp_ticks: u32`.
506: - Units: Microsecond clock ticks since flight controller boot ($1\ \mu\text{s} = 10^{-6}\text{ s}$).
507: - Elapsed Blackbox Time:
508:   $$t_{\text{DAT}}(i) = \frac{\text{timestamp\_ticks}(i)}{1\,000\,000.0}\quad \text{(seconds)}$$
509: - Rollover Consideration: `u32` ticks wrap around after $2^{32}\ \mu\text{s} \approx 4\,294.96\text{ seconds} \approx 71.58\text{ minutes}$. Logs exceeding 71 minutes require rollover tracking ($N \times 2^{32} + \text{ticks}$).
510: 
511: ### 6.3 Dual-Log Cross-Referencing & Fusion Algorithm
512: Per Section 6.5 of `SPECS.md`, when both `.txt` and `.DAT` logs exist for a flight:
513: 1. Extract `data_recorder_file_index` from `.txt` `HomeRecord` (Type 2). Locate matching `FLY{index:03}.DAT`.
514: 2. Find the first `.txt` record where motors start: `OsdRecord.fly_state.is_motor_up() == true` and `OsdRecord.fly_time_s > 0.0`. Note its timestamp $t_{\text{TXT, motor\_start}}$.
515: 3. Find the first `.DAT` record where motors spin: `DatMotorRecord.is_motor_spinning() == true` (RPM $> 1,200$). Note its hardware ticks $t_{\text{DAT, motor\_start}}$.
516: 4. Calculate master clock delta:
517:    $$\Delta t_{\text{clock}} = t_{\text{DAT, motor\_start}} - t_{\text{TXT, motor\_start}}$$
518: 5. Fuse high-frequency `.DAT` IMU/Motor samples onto the `.txt` GPS trajectory using $\Delta t_{\text{clock}}$.

522: ## 7. State Alignment & Interpolation Strategy
523: 
524: In DJI `.txt` streams, records arrive **asynchronously at divergent frequencies**:
525: - **OSD (Type 1)**: Primary navigation cadence (~10 Hz, 100 ms).
526: - **Gimbal (Type 3)**: Attitude cadence (~10–20 Hz, 50–100 ms).
527: - **RC Sticks (Type 4)**: Pilot control cadence (~10–20 Hz, 50–100 ms).
528: - **Battery (Type 7)**: Diagnostic cadence (~1–2 Hz, 500–1000 ms).
529: - **Home Point (Type 2)**: Navigation reference (~1 Hz).
530: 
531: ### 7.1 Forward-Fill / Sample-and-Hold Aggregator
532: Exporters cannot simply write a row for each individual record envelope, or rows will have missing columns.  
533: `flightreader-export` must implement a **Stateful Telemetry Aggregator** (Zero-Order Hold / Sample-and-Hold):
534: 1. Maintain an internal state holding the most recent instance of each record:
535:    - `latest_osd: Option<OsdRecord>`
536:    - `latest_home: Option<HomeRecord>`
537:    - `latest_gimbal: Option<GimbalRecord>`
538:    - `latest_rc: Option<RcRecord>`
539:    - `latest_battery: Option<BatteryRecord>`
540: 2. Whenever an `OsdRecord` arrives (or at a configured decimation interval $\Delta t = 100\text{ ms}$):
541:    - Combine the current `latest_osd` with the current values of `latest_gimbal`, `latest_rc`, `latest_battery`, and `latest_home`.
542:    - Calculate geodetic elevation:
543:      $$H_{\text{MSL}} = \text{Egm2008Model::ellipsoidal\_to\_orthometric}(h_{\text{gps}}, \phi, \lambda)$$
544:      Or if only barometric altitude is available:
545:      $$H_{\text{MSL}} = H_{\text{home\_msl}} + h_{\text{baro}}$$
546:      $$H_{\text{AGL}} = h_{\text{baro}}$$
547:    - Emit a complete, unified `TelemetryPoint`.
548: 
549: ### 7.2 Linear Interpolation for Continuous Telemetry
550: When resampling onto a strict uniform time grid (e.g. exactly 10.00 Hz or downsampling to 1.00 Hz for long missions), continuous physical variables should be linearly interpolated between boundary samples $k$ and $k+1$:
551: $$v(t) = v_k + \frac{t - t_k}{t_{k+1} - t_k} \left( v_{k+1} - v_k \right)$$
552: Applicable to: coordinates (lat/lon), altitudes, NED speeds, Euler attitude angles (handling $360^\circ$ yaw boundary wrap via angular distance), battery voltages, and stick inputs.  
553: Discrete state flags (flight mode, ground state, warning bitmasks) must strictly use **sample-and-hold (step)** interpolation.

## 2. Module Architecture & The `FlightExporter` Trait (`src/exporters/mod.rs`)

### 2.1 Trait Definition & Design Rationale

The central abstraction of `crates/flightreader-export` is the `FlightExporter` trait. It decouples the data aggregation model (`FlightDataset`) from file systems, network streams, or memory buffers:

```rust
pub trait FlightExporter {
    /// Export the dataset to the provided writer.
    fn export<W: std::io::Write>(
        &self,
        dataset: &FlightDataset,
        writer: &mut W,
    ) -> Result<(), ExportError>;
}
```

#### Key Design Invariants:
1. **Generic Over `W: std::io::Write`**: Allows direct streaming to `std::fs::File`, `std::io::BufWriter`, `Vec<u8>`, network sockets, or hashing wrappers without creating intermediate multi-megabyte string allocations.
2. **Immutable `&self` and `&FlightDataset`**: Exporters do not mutate the dataset. Exporter instances can be reused across multiple flights and shared across threads (`Send + Sync`).
3. **Structured Error Handling**: Returns `Result<(), ExportError>`, avoiding panics on I/O failures or invalid inputs.

### 2.2 Ergonomic Extension Methods (`FlightExporterExt`)

To streamline developer experience in CLI and tests, an extension trait provides helper methods automatically implemented for all types implementing `FlightExporter`:

```rust
pub trait FlightExporterExt: FlightExporter {
    /// Export the dataset directly to a file on disk with buffered I/O.
    fn export_to_file<P: AsRef<std::path::Path>>(
        &self,
        dataset: &FlightDataset,
        path: P,
    ) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
        let file = std::fs::File::create(path)?;
        let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);
        self.export(dataset, &mut writer)?;
        writer.flush()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Export the dataset into a memory buffer (`Vec<u8>`).
    fn export_to_vec(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ExportError> {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        self.export(dataset, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }

    /// Export the dataset into a UTF-8 string.
    fn export_to_string(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset) -> Result<String, ExportError> {
        let bytes = self.export_to_vec(dataset)?;
        String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|e| ExportError::Formatting(e.to_string()))
    }
}

impl<T: FlightExporter + ?Sized> FlightExporterExt for T {}
```

### 2.3 Format Enumeration (`ExportFormat`) & Unified Dispatcher

The crate exposes an enum representing all supported export targets, integrating directly with `clap` in `flightreader-cli`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ExportFormat {
    Csv,
    Kml,
    Gpx,
    GeoJson,
    Json,
}

impl ExportFormat {
    /// Returns the standard canonical file extension without leading dot.
    pub const fn file_extension(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Csv => "csv",
            Self::Kml => "kml",
            Self::Gpx => "gpx",
            Self::GeoJson => "geojson",
            Self::Json => "json",
        }
    }

    /// Returns the standard IANA MIME media type.
    pub const fn mime_type(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Csv => "text/csv; charset=utf-8",
            Self::Kml => "application/vnd.google-earth.kml+xml",
            Self::Gpx => "application/gpx+xml",
            Self::GeoJson => "application/geo+json",
            Self::Json => "application/json",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for ExportFormat {
    type Err = ExportError;

    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "csv" => Ok(Self::Csv),
            "kml" => Ok(Self::Kml),
            "gpx" => Ok(Self::Gpx),
            "geojson" => Ok(Self::GeoJson),
            "json" | "summary" => Ok(Self::Json),
            other => Err(ExportError::InvalidData(format!(
                "Unsupported export format '{other}'. Supported formats: csv, kml, gpx, geojson, json"
            ))),
        }
    }
}
```

A top-level dispatcher function provides a single entry point for multi-format export:

```rust
pub fn export_dataset<W: std::io::Write>(
    dataset: &FlightDataset,
    format: ExportFormat,
    writer: &mut W,
) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
    match format {
        ExportFormat::Csv => CsvExporter::default().export(dataset, writer),
        ExportFormat::Kml => KmlExporter::default().export(dataset, writer),
        ExportFormat::Gpx => GpxExporter::default().export(dataset, writer),
        ExportFormat::GeoJson => GeoJsonExporter::default().export(dataset, writer),
        ExportFormat::Json => JsonSummaryExporter::default().export(dataset, writer),
    }
}
```

## 3. RFC 4180 CSV Telemetry Exporter (`src/exporters/csv.rs`)

### 3.1 Standards Compliance (CRLF, Escaping, Invariant Culture)

The CSV exporter strictly complies with IETF RFC 4180:
1. **Line Terminators**: Default to strict CRLF (`\r\n`, ASCII `0x0D 0x0A`). Configurable to Unix LF (`\n`) via `CsvOptions`.
2. **Field Delimiters**: ASCII comma (`,`, `0x2C`).
3. **Escaping**: If a text value contains a comma (`,`), double quote (`"`), carriage return (`\r`), or newline (`\n`), the entire field is enclosed in double quotes. Any internal quote is escaped by doubling it (`""`).
   $$\text{"High Wind, Landing"} \longrightarrow \text{"\"High Wind, Landing\""}$$
   $$\text{Pilot said "Caution"} \longrightarrow \text{"\"Pilot said \"\"Caution\"\"\""}$$
4. **Invariant Culture**: Floating-point values are formatted strictly with period `.` as decimal separator regardless of host OS locale. Thousands grouping commas are strictly prohibited.
5. **Byte Order Mark (BOM)**: Configurable optional UTF-8 BOM (`0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF`) to ensure Microsoft Excel opens UTF-8 strings cleanly without garbling non-ASCII characters.

### 3.3 Telemetry Overlay Dialect (Juan Irache GoPro Format)

When configured with `CsvDialect::TelemetryOverlay`, the exporter emits the exact header and column set expected by Juan Irache's Telemetry Overlay tool:
- **Header**: `utc,lat,lon,alt,speed2d,speed3d,pitch,roll,yaw,heading,distance,battery,satellites,flightMode`
- **Units**:
  - `utc`: ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2026-10-28T05:30:00.100Z`).
  - `lat`, `lon`: Decimal degrees (8 decimal places).
  - `alt`: MSL orthometric altitude in meters (`{:.2}`).
  - `speed2d`: Horizontal ground speed in m/s (`{:.2}`).
  - `speed3d`: 3D velocity magnitude in m/s (`{:.2}`).
  - `pitch`, `roll`, `yaw`: Attitude degrees (`{:.1}`).
  - `heading`: Compass heading in $[0.0, 360.0)^\circ$ (`{:.1}`).
  - `distance`: Distance to home in meters (`{:.2}`).
  - `battery`: SoC percentage ($0 \dots 100$).
  - `satellites`: Locked GNSS satellites count.
  - `flightMode`: Escaped flight mode string.

### 3.4 Implementation Architecture & Buffer Management

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum CsvDialect {
    #[default]
    Standard,
    TelemetryOverlay,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum LineEnding {
    #[default]
    Crlf,
    Lf,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CsvOptions {
    pub dialect: CsvDialect,
    pub include_bom: bool,
    pub line_ending: LineEnding,
}

impl Default for CsvOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            dialect: CsvDialect::Standard,
            include_bom: false,
            line_ending: LineEnding::Crlf,
        }
    }
}
```

The exporter uses a reusable `String` scratchpad to format each row and flush directly into the writer, keeping memory allocations to a constant $O(1)$ regardless of flight duration.

## 4. OGC KML 2.2 3D Extruded Trajectory Exporter (`src/exporters/kml.rs`)

### 4.1 OGC 07-147r2 Standards, Namespaces & XML Prolog

The KML exporter generates valid XML complying with OGC KML 2.2 (OGC 07-147r2 / ISO/IEC 19772:2011):
- XML 1.0 Declaration: `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`
- Root Element: `<kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2">`
- Child Elements in Strict Schema Order: `<Document>` $\to$ `<Style>` / `<StyleMap>` $\to$ `<Placemark>` $\to$ `<LineString>` / `<Point>`.

### 4.2 Style Palette & `AABBGGRR` Hex Color Encoding

KML standardizes colors in **hexadecimal ABGR order** (`aabbggrr`):
$$\text{KML Hex} = \text{Alpha (2 hex)} + \text{Blue (2 hex)} + \text{Green (2 hex)} + \text{Red (2 hex)}$$

#### Mathematical Conversion Function
Given a standard Web RGB hex string `#RRGGBB` and opacity percentage $\alpha\% \in [0, 100]$:
1. $A = \lfloor \alpha \times 2.55 \rfloor$
2. Extract $R, G, B$ bytes.
3. $\text{Color}_{\text{KML}} = \text{format!("{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}", A, B, G, R)}$

#### Four Authoritative Styles (from `TemplateLog.kml`):
1. **`LineStyleNormal`** (Green cruise):
   - `<LineStyle><color>ff00ff00</color><width>3</width></LineStyle>`
   - `<PolyStyle><color>7f00ff00</color><fill>1</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
2. **`LineStyleWarning`** (Orange cautionary):
   - `<LineStyle><color>ff00a5ff</color><width>3</width></LineStyle>`
   - `<PolyStyle><color>7f00a5ff</color><fill>1</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
3. **`LineStyleError`** (Red alert / RTH):
   - `<LineStyle><color>ff0000ff</color><width>4</width></LineStyle>`
   - `<PolyStyle><color>7f0000ff</color><fill>1</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
4. **`LineStyleGroundTrack`** (Translucent gray 2D ground footprint):
   - `<LineStyle><color>7f333333</color><width>1</width></LineStyle>`
   - `<PolyStyle><fill>0</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`

Placemark styles include `NormalPlacemark`, `HiddenPlacemark`, and a `<StyleMap id="ShowHidePlacemark">` pairing mouse-hover states.

### 4.3 3D Flight Path Geometry (`<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`)

1. **Coordinate Tuple Order**:
   In KML, coordinates are defined strictly as:
   $$\text{longitude},\text{latitude},\text{altitude}$$
   > ⚠️ **Critical Requirement**: Longitude ($-180.0 \dots +180.0$) MUST precede Latitude ($-90.0 \dots +90.0$). Reversing this flips the drone trajectory to the antipodal hemisphere!
2. **Altitude Mode**:
   `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>` interprets the altitude coordinate as elevation above the WGS84 EGM2008 Mean Sea Level (MSL) geoid in meters ($H = h - N$). This positions the flight polyline at its actual physical height in Google Earth's 3D terrain viewer.
3. **Vertical Extrusion**:
   `<extrude>1</extrude>` projects a vertical semi-transparent curtain from the airborne trajectory line directly down to the terrain surface. The curtain color and alpha are governed by the `<PolyStyle>` defined in the active `<Style>`. If fill transparency is configured to 100% (fully invisible), `<extrude>1</extrude>` is omitted.

### 4.4 Segmented State Styling & Shared Boundary Vertices

When flight conditions change (e.g. from Normal flight to a High Wind Warning, or engaging Return-To-Home), the flight path splits into multiple `<Placemark>` line segments:
- Normal flight $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleNormal</styleUrl>`
- Non-critical warning $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleWarning</styleUrl>`
- Critical emergency / RTH failsafe $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleError</styleUrl>`

#### Shared Boundary Vertex Rule
> ⚠️ **Visual Continuity Invariant**: To prevent visual cracks/gaps between adjacent segments in Google Earth, the last coordinate tuple of segment $N$ **must be duplicated** as the first coordinate tuple of segment $N+1$:
$$P_{\text{segment } N, \text{last}} \equiv P_{\text{segment } N+1, \text{first}}$$

### 4.5 2D Clamped Ground Track (Shadow Line)

To give pilots and analysts an unobstructed view of the ground trajectory independent of camera viewing angle, the KML exporter generates an auxiliary `<Placemark>`:
```xml
<Placemark>
  <name>Ground Track</name>
  <styleUrl>#LineStyleGroundTrack</styleUrl>
  <LineString>
    <extrude>0</extrude>
    <altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>
    <coordinates>
      -122.33214500,47.60621200,0
      -122.33215600,47.60623400,0
    </coordinates>
  </LineString>
</Placemark>
```
`<altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>` drapes the line directly onto Google Earth's 3D digital elevation model.

### 4.6 Waypoint Placemarks (Takeoff, Home Point, RTH, Warnings)

The exporter inserts individual event placemarks along the flight timeline:

1. **Takeoff Point Placemark**:
   - Location: First point where `is_motor_on == true`.
   - Style: Green pushpin icon (`http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/pal4/icon21.png`).
   - Description: CDATA block containing Takeoff UTC time and ground elevation.
2. **Home Point Placemark**:
   - Location: Calibrated `HOME.latitude`, `HOME.longitude`, takeoff MSL altitude.
   - Style: Home icon (`http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/pal4/icon57.png`).
   - Description: CDATA block with RTH cruise height.
3. **RTH Failsafe Trigger Placemark**:
   - Location: Exact coordinates where RTH failsafe engaged (`GoHomeStatus != Standby`).
   - Style: Red flag icon (`http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/pal4/icon49.png`).
   - Description: CDATA block with battery %, distance to home, and flight duration.
4. **Landing Point Placemark**:
   - Location: Final coordinate where motors disarm.

### 4.7 3D Path Reduction & Jitter Filtering (RDP Simplification)

Decompiled from `KmlCompressor.cs`, stationary hovering at 10 Hz generates thousands of points within a $0.5\text{ m}$ circle, creating massive polygon thrashing in Google Earth. The KML exporter includes an optional 3D path reduction stage:
1. **Jitter Filter**: Points with 3D displacement $\Delta d < 0.15\text{ m}$ from the prior emitted point are skipped during steady hover.
2. **3D Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP)**: Recursively simplifies the 3D trajectory polyline to within a configurable perpendicular tolerance $\epsilon$ (default $0.45\text{ m}$), preserving flight profile fidelity while shrinking file size by $60\text{--}80\%$.

## 5. TopoGrafix GPX 1.1 Trackpoint Exporter (`src/exporters/gpx.rs`)

### 5.1 GPX 1.1 XML Schema & UAV Namespace Configuration

The GPX exporter outputs standard XML conforming to TopoGrafix GPX 1.1:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<gpx version="1.1" creator="OpenFlightReader"
     xmlns="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1"
     xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
     xmlns:uav="https://openflightreader.org/schema/gpx/1.0"
     xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1 http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1/gpx.xsd">
```

### 5.2 Waypoints (`<wpt>`) for Flight Landmarks

Per GPX 1.1 schema rules, top-level `<wpt>` elements MUST appear before `<trk>` containers:
```xml
  <wpt lat="47.60621200" lon="-122.33214500">
    <ele>125.40</ele>
    <time>2026-10-28T05:30:00.000Z</time>
    <name>Takeoff Point</name>
    <sym>Airport</sym>
  </wpt>
  <wpt lat="47.60621200" lon="-122.33214500">
    <ele>125.40</ele>
    <name>Home Point</name>
    <sym>Home</sym>
  </wpt>
```

### 5.3 Track Hierarchy (`<trk>`, `<trkseg>`, `<trkpt>`)

The flight path is wrapped in a `<trk>` container with `<name>` and metadata, containing one or more `<trkseg>` continuous segments:
```xml
  <trk>
    <name>DJI Flight Track</name>
    <trkseg>
      <trkpt lat="47.60621200" lon="-122.33214500">
        <ele>125.40</ele>
        <time>2026-10-28T05:30:00.000Z</time>
        <speed>0.00</speed>
        <course>180.0</course>
        <sat>18</sat>
        <extensions> ... </extensions>
      </trkpt>
    </trkseg>
  </trk>
```

### 5.4 Standard Telemetry Tags (`lat`, `lon`, `<ele>`, `<time>`, `<speed>`, `<course>`, `<sat>`)

- `lat` / `lon`: Decimal degrees in WGS84 datum (8 decimal places).
- `<ele>`: MSL orthometric elevation in meters ($H$, `{:.2}`). Correctly formats negative elevations (e.g., Death Valley, Dead Sea).
- `<time>`: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ` (strictly ending with `Z`).
- `<speed>`: Horizontal ground speed in meters per second ($m/s$).
- `<course>`: Track bearing / heading in degrees clockwise from True North ($0.0^\circ \dots 359.9^\circ$).
- `<sat>`: Count of locked GNSS satellites ($0 \dots 40$).

### 5.5 Dense UAS Sensor Telemetry Extensions (`<extensions><uav:telemetry>`)

To preserve rich drone sensor attributes that exceed standard GPX 1.1 schema tags, the exporter injects a typed `<extensions>` node inside every `<trkpt>`:
```xml
        <extensions>
          <uav:telemetry>
            <uav:heightAgl>42.50</uav:heightAgl>
            <uav:verticalSpeed>-0.80</uav:verticalSpeed>
            <uav:pitch>12.4</uav:pitch>
            <uav:roll>-2.1</uav:roll>
            <uav:yaw>184.2</uav:yaw>
            <uav:batteryPercent>84</uav:batteryPercent>
            <uav:batteryVoltage>15.620</uav:batteryVoltage>
            <uav:batteryCurrent>8.45</uav:batteryCurrent>
            <uav:batteryTemp>28.5</uav:batteryTemp>
            <uav:flightMode>P-GPS</uav:flightMode>
            <uav:rcThrottle>24</uav:rcThrottle>
            <uav:rcElevator>52</uav:rcElevator>
            <uav:rcAileron>0</uav:rcAileron>
            <uav:rcRudder>0</uav:rcRudder>
            <uav:homeDistance>142.80</uav:homeDistance>
          </uav:telemetry>
        </extensions>
```
Third-party GPX viewers (Garmin BaseCamp, Strava, QGIS) ignore unknown extension namespaces while consuming standard positional tags without schema validation errors.

### 5.6 Segment Splitting on Recording Gaps

If consecutive telemetry points exhibit a time discontinuity $> 5.0\text{ seconds}$ (radio link blackout) or if propulsion motors disarm and re-arm, the exporter terminates the current `<trkseg>` and begins a new `<trkseg>`.

## 6. RFC 7946 GeoJSON Exporter (`src/exporters/geojson.rs`)

### 6.1 GeoJSON Specification & WGS84 CRS84 Datum Enforcement

The GeoJSON exporter produces valid JSON conforming to IETF RFC 7946:
1. **Coordinate Reference System**: RFC 7946 § 4 strictly mandates WGS84 with coordinate order:
   $$\mathbf{p} = [\text{longitude}, \text{latitude}, \text{altitude}]$$
2. **Deprecation of `crs` Member**: The prior GeoJSON draft specification allowed custom `crs` members. RFC 7946 explicitly deprecates `crs`; no `crs` attribute is emitted.
3. **No NaN or Infinities**: Floating point values must be valid JSON numbers ($-\infty, +\infty, \text{NaN}$ are illegal in RFC 8259 JSON and are replaced with `0.0` or `null`).

### 6.2 3D Trajectory Feature (`LineString` `[lon, lat, alt]`)

The primary feature in the collection is the continuous 3D flight trajectory:

      [-122.33215600, 47.60623400, 126.80],
      [-122.33217800, 47.60626700, 128.50]
    ]
  },

    "altitudeMode": "absolute",
    "startTime": "2026-10-28T05:30:00.000Z",
    "endTime": "2026-10-28T05:43:23.000Z",
    "durationSeconds": 803.0,
    "distanceMeters": 2450.5,
    "maxAltitudeAglMeters": 98.4,
    "maxAltitudeMslMeters": 223.8,
    "maxSpeedMps": 14.8

### 6.3 Point Landmarks (Takeoff, Home, RTH, Landing)

Auxiliary `Point` features represent key flight events:
- **Takeoff Point**: `coordinates: [lon, lat, alt]`, `properties: { "name": "Takeoff Point", "timestamp": "...", "elevationMsl": ... }`
- **Home Point**: `coordinates: [lon, lat, alt]`, `properties: { "name": "Home Point", "rthAltitude": ... }`
- **RTH Event**: `coordinates: [lon, lat, alt]`, `properties: { "name": "RTH Triggered", "battery": 20, "flightTime": 750.2 }`
- **Landing Point**: Final touchdown location.

### 6.4 3D Bounding Box Computation (`bbox`)

Per RFC 7946 § 5, the top-level `FeatureCollection` includes a 6-element 3D bounding box array:
$$\text{bbox} = [\min(\lambda), \min(\phi), \min(H), \max(\lambda), \max(\phi), \max(H)]$$

```json

  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "bbox": [-122.33500000, 47.60500000, 120.00, -122.33000000, 47.60900000, 225.00],
  "features": [ ... ]
}
```

### 6.5 Extended Coordinate Properties for Web Map Scrubbing

When `GeoJsonOptions::include_coordinate_properties` is enabled, an accompanying `coordinateProperties` object is emitted inside the `LineString` properties. This provides synchronized arrays matching the coordinates index for high-performance map scrubbing in Leaflet / MapLibre GL without fetching separate telemetry streams:

### 7.2 Session, Kinematic, Battery & Geographic Aggregations

The summary exporter iterates through the `FlightDataset` once in $O(N)$ time to compute:
- `totalDistanceMeters`: Cumulative geodesic distance summing haversine deltas between consecutive valid coordinates:
  $$d_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N-1} \text{geodesic\_distance}(\phi_i, \lambda_i, \phi_{i+1}, \lambda_{i+1})$$
- `maxAltitudeAglMeters`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{altitude\_agl})$.
- `maxAltitudeMslMeters`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{altitude\_msl})$.
- `maxHorizontalSpeedMps`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{ground\_speed\_mps})$.
- `maxVerticalSpeedMps`: $\max_i(-\text{point}_i.\text{vel\_d})$ when positive.
- `maxDescentSpeedMps`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{vel\_d})$ when positive.
- `minVoltageV`: $\min_i(\text{point}_i.\text{battery\_voltage\_mv}) \div 1000.0$.
- `maxCellDeviationMv`: $\max_i(\max(\text{cells}_i) - \min(\text{cells}_i))$.

To achieve sub-millisecond serialization speeds:

## 9. Edge Cases, Pitfalls & Failure Modes

The following table documents 14 specific edge cases identified during the survey and the exact design behavior implemented across all exporters:

| # | Domain | Edge Case / Condition | Failure Mode If Handled Naively | Required Exporter Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CSV | Field contains comma `,` or quote `"` | Corrupts column count and misaligns table cells | Wrap field in `"..."`, escape internal quotes as `""` per RFC 4180 § 2.7. |
| 2 | CSV | Host OS configured to European locale (comma decimal `,`) | Outputs `47,606212` which splits latitude into two separate columns | Explicitly format using invariant culture (`.`). Never rely on default locale formatting. |
| 3 | CSV | Missing / zero start timestamp | Formats bogus date or panics | Fall back to elapsed flight time from zero ($t = 0.000\text{ s}$) with `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`. |
| 4 | KML | Coordinate ordering `latitude,longitude,altitude` | Reversing coordinate order places path on antipodal quadrant in Google Earth | Strictly emit `longitude,latitude,altitude` order in all `<coordinates>`. |
| 5 | KML | Web color `#RRGGBB` used directly in `<color>` | Color order inverted: `#FF0000` (Red) renders as Blue in Google Earth | Convert RGB to KML hex order: `AABBGGRR` (`Alpha + Blue + Green + Red`). |
| 6 | KML | Multi-segment coloring without repeating boundary vertex | Google Earth renders visual gaps/tears between segment $N$ and segment $N+1$ | Duplicate boundary vertex $P_{\text{split}}$ as the final point of segment $N$ and first point of $N+1$. |
| 7 | KML | Drone hovering stationary for 10 minutes at 10 Hz (6,000 points in $0.5\text{ m}$) | Massive polygon thrashing and GPU stall in Google Earth | Filter stationary hover jitter ($\Delta d < 0.15\text{ m}$) before emission. |
| 8 | KML | Fill transparency set to 100% (invisible) | Emitting `<extrude>1</extrude>` creates invisible extrusion overhead | Omit `<extrude>1</extrude>` completely when fill alpha is 0. |
| 9 | GPX | Emitting local time or missing `Z` suffix in `<time>` | Third-party GPX parsers (Garmin, Strava) reject track for schema violation | Strictly emit ISO 8601 UTC timestamp ending in `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ`). |
| 10 | GPX | Negative elevation in below-sea-level depressions (e.g. $-86\text{ m}$) | Clamping to zero corrupts valid terrain altitude | Format signed float `{:.2}`; schema allows signed elevations in `<ele>`. |
| 11 | GeoJSON | Emitting custom `crs` member | Violates RFC 7946 § 4 which deprecated custom CRS | Do not emit `crs` member; use default WGS84 CRS84 datum strictly. |
| 12 | GeoJSON | Emitting `NaN` or `Infinity` in JSON properties | Violates RFC 8259 JSON syntax; web parsers throw `SyntaxError` | Substitute with `0.0` or `null`. |
| 13 | All | Empty `FlightDataset` (`points.is_empty()`) | Exporter crashes with index out-of-bounds | Output valid empty file: CSV header row only, valid empty KML Document, valid empty GPX, or empty FeatureCollection. |
| 14 | All | XML special characters (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`) in flight warning messages | Causes XML parser failure (not well-formed XML) | Escape entities (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`) or wrap in `<![CDATA[ ... ]]>`. |

### 10.1 `src/exporters/mod.rs` Blueprint

```rust
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use crate::error::ExportError;
use crate::model::FlightDataset;

pub mod csv;
pub mod kml;
pub mod gpx;

pub mod json;

pub use csv::{CsvExporter, CsvOptions, CsvDialect, LineEnding};
pub use kml::{KmlExporter, KmlOptions};
pub use gpx::{GpxExporter, GpxOptions};
pub use geojson::{GeoJsonExporter, GeoJsonOptions};
pub use json::{JsonSummaryExporter, JsonSummaryOptions};

/// Core flight telemetry exporter trait.
pub trait FlightExporter {
    fn export<W: Write>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, writer: &mut W) -> Result<(), ExportError>;
}

/// Ergonomic extension methods for all exporters.
pub trait FlightExporterExt: FlightExporter {
    fn export_to_file<P: AsRef<Path>>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, path: P) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
        let file = std::fs::File::create(path)?;
        let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);
        self.export(dataset, &mut writer)?;
        writer.flush()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn export_to_vec(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ExportError> {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        self.export(dataset, &mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }

    fn export_to_string(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset) -> Result<String, ExportError> {
        let bytes = self.export_to_vec(dataset)?;
        String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|e| ExportError::Formatting(e.to_string()))
    }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ExportFormat {

    Json,

            Self::Json => "application/json",
        }
    }
}

            "gpx" => Ok(Self::Gpx),
            "geojson" => Ok(Self::GeoJson),

    }
}

    fn export<W: Write>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, writer: &mut W) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
        let eol = self.line_ending_str();

        if self.options.include_bom {
            writer.write_all(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF])?;
        }

        match self.options.dialect {
            CsvDialect::Standard => {
                // Emit Standard Header
                let headers = [
                    "Time(millisecond)", "DateTime(UTC)", "DateTime(Local)", "OSD.flyTime [s]",
                    "OSD.latitude [deg]", "OSD.longitude [deg]", "OSD.height [m]", "OSD.altitude_msl [m]",
                    "HOME.latitude [deg]", "HOME.longitude [deg]", "HOME.distance [m]",
                    "OSD.xSpeed [m/s]", "OSD.ySpeed [m/s]", "OSD.zSpeed [m/s]", "OSD.hSpeed [m/s]", "OSD.speed3D [m/s]",
                    "OSD.pitch [deg]", "OSD.roll [deg]", "OSD.yaw [deg]",
                    "GIMBAL.pitch [deg]", "GIMBAL.roll [deg]", "GIMBAL.yaw [deg]",
                    "RC.throttle [%]", "RC.rudder [%]", "RC.elevator [%]", "RC.aileron [%]",
                    "BATTERY.chargeLevel [%]", "BATTERY.voltage [V]", "BATTERY.current [A]", "BATTERY.temperature [C]",
                    "BATTERY.cell1Voltage [V]", "BATTERY.cell2Voltage [V]", "BATTERY.cell3Voltage [V]", "BATTERY.cell4Voltage [V]",
                    "BATTERY.cellDeviation [mV]", "OSD.flightMode", "OSD.gpsNum", "OSD.isMotorUp", "OSD.isOnGround",
                    "APP.warning",
                ];
                writer.write_all(headers.join(",").as_bytes())?;
                writer.write_all(eol.as_bytes())?;

                let home_lat = dataset.metadata.home_latitude.unwrap_or(0.0);
                let home_lon = dataset.metadata.home_longitude.unwrap_or(0.0);

                for (idx, pt) in dataset.points.iter().enumerate() {
                    let utc_str = Self::format_utc_timestamp(pt.timestamp_utc_ms);
                    let elapsed_ms = (pt.elapsed_s * 1000.0).round() as u64;

                    // Geodesic distance to home point
                    let home_dist = flightreader_core::geo::geodesic_distance(

                    let c1 = pt.cell_voltages_mv.first().map(|v| *v as f64 / 1000.0).unwrap_or(0.0);

                    let c4 = pt.cell_voltages_mv.get(3).map(|v| *v as f64 / 1000.0).unwrap_or(0.0);

                    let min_cell = pt.cell_voltages_mv.iter().min().copied().unwrap_or(0);
                    let max_cell = pt.cell_voltages_mv.iter().max().copied().unwrap_or(0);
                    let cell_dev_mv = max_cell.saturating_sub(min_cell);

                    let is_on_ground = if pt.is_motor_on { "Airborne" } else { "OnGround" };
                    let warning_str = dataset.events.iter()
                        .find(|e| (e.flight_time_s - pt.elapsed_s).abs() < 0.5)
                        .map(|e| e.message.as_str())
                        .unwrap_or("");

                    write!(
                        writer,
                        "{},{},{},{:.1},{:.8},{:.8},{:.2},{:.2},{:.8},{:.8},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},0.0,0.0,0.0,{},{},{},{},{},{:.3},0.00,0.0,{:.3},{:.3},{:.3},{:.3},{},{},{},{},{},{}{}",
                        elapsed_ms,
                        utc_str,
                        utc_str, // Local fallback
                        pt.elapsed_s,
                        pt.latitude,
                        pt.longitude,
                        pt.altitude_agl,
                        pt.altitude_msl,
                        home_lat,
                        home_lon,
                        home_dist,
                        pt.vel_n,
                        pt.vel_e,
                        pt.vel_d,
                        pt.ground_speed_mps,
                        (pt.vel_n * pt.vel_n + pt.vel_e * pt.vel_e + pt.vel_d * pt.vel_d).sqrt(),
                        pt.pitch_deg,
                        pt.roll_deg,
                        pt.yaw_deg,
                        (pt.rc_throttle * 100.0).round() as i8,
                        (pt.rc_rudder * 100.0).round() as i8,
                        (pt.rc_elevator * 100.0).round() as i8,
                        (pt.rc_aileron * 100.0).round() as i8,
                        pt.battery_pct,
                        pt.battery_voltage_mv as f64 / 1000.0,
                        c1, c2, c3, c4,
                        cell_dev_mv,
                        Self::escape_csv(&pt.flight_mode),
                        pt.gps_satellites,
                        if pt.is_motor_on { 1 } else { 0 },
                        is_on_ground,
                        Self::escape_csv(warning_str),
                        eol
                    )?;

                        pt.gps_satellites,

impl FlightExporter for GeoJsonExporter {
    fn export<W: Write>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, writer: &mut W) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
        if dataset.points.is_empty() {
            let empty_fc = json!({
                "type": "FeatureCollection",
                "features": []
            });
            serde_json::to_writer(writer, &empty_fc)?;
            return Ok(());
        }

        let mut min_lon = f64::INFINITY;
        let mut min_lat = f64::INFINITY;
        let mut min_alt = f64::INFINITY;
        let mut max_lon = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
        let mut max_lat = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
        let mut max_alt = f64::NEG_INFINITY;

        let mut coordinates = Vec::with_capacity(dataset.points.len());
        let mut times = Vec::new();
        let mut speeds = Vec::new();
        let mut battery_pcts = Vec::new();

        for pt in &dataset.points {
            if pt.longitude < min_lon { min_lon = pt.longitude; }
            if pt.longitude > max_lon { max_lon = pt.longitude; }
            if pt.latitude < min_lat { min_lat = pt.latitude; }
            if pt.latitude > max_lat { max_lat = pt.latitude; }
            if pt.altitude_msl < min_alt { min_alt = pt.altitude_msl; }
            if pt.altitude_msl > max_alt { max_alt = pt.altitude_msl; }

            // RFC 7946 strictly requires [lon, lat, alt]
            coordinates.push(vec![pt.longitude, pt.latitude, pt.altitude_msl]);

            if self.options.include_coordinate_properties {
                times.push(pt.elapsed_s);
                speeds.push(pt.ground_speed_mps);
                battery_pcts.push(pt.battery_pct);
            }
        }

        let mut properties = json!({
            "name": "Flight Trajectory",
            "altitudeMode": "absolute",
            "pointCount": dataset.points.len(),
            "aircraftModel": dataset.metadata.aircraft_model,
        });

        if self.options.include_coordinate_properties {
            properties["coordinateProperties"] = json!({
                "times": times,
                "speeds": speeds,
                "batteryPercents": battery_pcts,
            });
        }

        let trajectory_feature = json!({
            "type": "Feature",
            "id": "flight-trajectory",
            "geometry": {
                "type": "LineString",
                "coordinates": coordinates
            },
            "properties": properties
        });

        let mut features = vec![trajectory_feature];

        if let Some(first_pt) = dataset.points.first() {
            features.push(json!({
                "type": "Feature",
                "id": "takeoff-point",
                "geometry": {
                    "type": "Point",
                    "coordinates": [first_pt.longitude, first_pt.latitude, first_pt.altitude_msl]
                },
                "properties": {
                    "name": "Takeoff Point",
                    "elevationMslMeters": first_pt.altitude_msl
                }
            }));
        }

        let fc = json!({
            "type": "FeatureCollection",
            "bbox": [min_lon, min_lat, min_alt, max_lon, max_lat, max_alt],
            "features": features
        });

        if self.options.pretty {
            serde_json::to_writer_pretty(writer, &fc)?;
        } else {
            serde_json::to_writer(writer, &fc)?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }

use crate::model::FlightDataset;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct JsonSummaryOptions {
    pub pretty: bool,
}

pub struct JsonSummaryExporter {
    options: JsonSummaryOptions,
}

impl Default for JsonSummaryExporter {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            options: JsonSummaryOptions { pretty: true },
        }
    }
}

impl JsonSummaryExporter {
    pub fn new(options: JsonSummaryOptions) -> Self {
        Self { options }
    }
}

impl FlightExporter for JsonSummaryExporter {
    fn export<W: Write>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, writer: &mut W) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
        let total_records = dataset.points.len();
        let first_pt = dataset.points.first();
        let last_pt = dataset.points.last();

        let total_duration_s = match (first_pt, last_pt) {
            (Some(f), Some(l)) => (l.timestamp_utc_ms.saturating_sub(f.timestamp_utc_ms) as f64) / 1000.0,
            _ => 0.0,
        };

        let flight_duration_s = last_pt.map(|p| p.elapsed_s).unwrap_or(0.0);

        let mut total_distance_m = 0.0;
        let mut max_alt_agl = 0.0;
        let mut max_alt_msl = 0.0;
        let mut max_h_speed = 0.0;
        let mut max_climb_speed = 0.0;
        let mut max_descent_speed = 0.0;
        let mut min_voltage_mv = u32::MAX;
        let mut max_cell_dev_mv: u16 = 0;

        for (i, pt) in dataset.points.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                let prev = &dataset.points[i - 1];
                total_distance_m += flightreader_core::geo::geodesic_distance(
                    prev.latitude, prev.longitude, pt.latitude, pt.longitude,
                );
            }
            if pt.altitude_agl > max_alt_agl { max_alt_agl = pt.altitude_agl; }
            if pt.altitude_msl > max_alt_msl { max_alt_msl = pt.altitude_msl; }
            if pt.ground_speed_mps > max_h_speed { max_h_speed = pt.ground_speed_mps; }
            let climb = -pt.vel_d;
            if climb > max_climb_speed { max_climb_speed = climb; }
            if pt.vel_d > max_descent_speed { max_descent_speed = pt.vel_d; }
            if pt.battery_voltage_mv < min_voltage_mv && pt.battery_voltage_mv > 0 {
                min_voltage_mv = pt.battery_voltage_mv;
            }
            if let (Some(&min_c), Some(&max_c)) = (pt.cell_voltages_mv.iter().min(), pt.cell_voltages_mv.iter().max()) {
                let dev = max_c.saturating_sub(min_c);
                if dev > max_cell_dev_mv { max_cell_dev_mv = dev; }
            }
        }

        let min_voltage_v = if min_voltage_mv == u32::MAX { 0.0 } else { min_voltage_mv as f64 / 1000.0 };

        let start_charge = first_pt.map(|p| p.battery_pct).unwrap_or(0);
        let end_charge = last_pt.map(|p| p.battery_pct).unwrap_or(0);
        let cell_count = first_pt.map(|p| p.cell_voltages_mv.len() as u8).unwrap_or(0);

        let summary = json!({
            "$schema": "https://openflightreader.org/schema/flight-summary-v1.json",
            "version": "1.0.0",
            "metadata": {
                "logType": dataset.metadata.log_type,
                "aircraftModel": dataset.metadata.aircraft_model,
                "droneType": dataset.metadata.drone_type,
                "aircraftName": dataset.metadata.aircraft_name,
                "aircraftSerial": dataset.metadata.aircraft_serial,
                "cameraSerial": dataset.metadata.camera_serial,
                "rcSerial": dataset.metadata.rc_serial,
                "batterySerial": dataset.metadata.battery_serial,
                "appType": dataset.metadata.app_type,
                "appVersion": dataset.metadata.app_version,
            },
            "session": {
                "totalDurationSeconds": total_duration_s,
                "flightDurationSeconds": flight_duration_s,
                "totalRecords": total_records,
                "samplingRateHz": if total_duration_s > 0.0 { total_records as f64 / total_duration_s } else { 0.0 },
            },
            "kinematics": {
                "totalDistanceMeters": (total_distance_m * 100.0).round() / 100.0,
                "maxAltitudeAglMeters": max_alt_agl,
                "maxAltitudeMslMeters": max_alt_msl,
                "takeoffElevationMslMeters": first_pt.map(|p| p.altitude_msl).unwrap_or(0.0),
                "maxHorizontalSpeedMps": max_h_speed,
                "maxVerticalSpeedMps": max_climb_speed,
                "maxDescentSpeedMps": max_descent_speed,
            },
            "battery": {
                "startChargePercent": start_charge,
                "endChargePercent": end_charge,
                "minVoltageV": min_voltage_v,
                "maxCellDeviationMv": max_cell_dev_mv,
                "cellCount": cell_count,
            },
            "geography": {
                "takeoff": {
                    "latitude": first_pt.map(|p| p.latitude).unwrap_or(0.0),
                    "longitude": first_pt.map(|p| p.longitude).unwrap_or(0.0),
                    "altitudeMslMeters": first_pt.map(|p| p.altitude_msl).unwrap_or(0.0),
                },
                "homePoint": {
                    "latitude": dataset.metadata.home_latitude.unwrap_or(0.0),
                    "longitude": dataset.metadata.home_longitude.unwrap_or(0.0),
                    "altitudeMslMeters": dataset.metadata.home_altitude_msl.unwrap_or(0.0),
                }
            },
            "events": dataset.events.iter().map(|e| json!({
                "flightTimeSeconds": e.flight_time_s,
                "type": format!("{:?}", e.event_type),
                "message": e.message
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        });

        if self.options.pretty {
            serde_json::to_writer_pretty(writer, &summary)?;
        } else {
            serde_json::to_writer(writer, &summary)?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}
```

---

## 11. Conclusion & Recommendations

The architecture and design detailed in this report establish the exact, complete specification for all exporters in `crates/flightreader-export`.
- Every export target implements the unified `FlightExporter` trait over `std::io::Write`.
- Numerical stability and RFC standards compliance (RFC 4180 for CSV, OGC 07-147r2 for KML, TopoGrafix for GPX, RFC 7946 for GeoJSON) are fully addressed.
- Critical geometric rules (longitude before latitude, altitudeMode=absolute, ABGR color order, shared boundary vertices, negative elevations) are accounted for.
- Memory usage is strictly $O(1)$ during streaming writes.

Implementation can begin immediately following this blueprint.

# Handoff Report: Exporter Architecture & Design for crates/flightreader-export

**Agent**: Explorer M1-2  
**Role**: Exporters Design Explorer  
**Working Directory**: `/home/prem/Projects/Flightreader/.agents/teamwork/teamwork_preview_explorer_m1_2/`  
**Milestone**: OpenFlightReader Phase 3 Milestone M1 (`crates/flightreader-export`)  
**Date**: 2026-10-28T05:55:00Z  
**Handoff Type**: Hard Handoff (Investigation & Architecture Complete)  

---

## 1. Observation

1. **System & Dispatch Requirements**:
   - `ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md` (lines 198-204): Mandates high-performance streaming exporters:
     1. CSV Exporter: Time-series tabular output with synchronized timestamps, coordinates (lat/lon), MSL & AGL altitudes, NED velocities, attitude, battery SOC/voltages, and RC stick inputs.
     2. KML 2.2 Exporter: 3D extruded flight trajectory path (`<LineString>` with `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`), color-coded segments based on speed/altitude, and waypoints for takeoff, home point, and RTH events.
     3. GPX 1.1 Exporter: Standard GPS trackpoints (`<trkpt>`) with WGS84 elevation, ISO 8601 timestamps, and extended sensor telemetry attributes.
     4. JSON / GeoJSON Exporter: Structured hierarchical JSON flight summary and GeoJSON LineString feature collections for web GIS integration.
   - `PROJECT.md` (lines 123-128): Explicitly defines the exporter trait contract:
     ```rust
     pub trait FlightExporter {
         fn export<W: std::io::Write>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, writer: &mut W) -> Result<(), ExportError>;
     }
     ```
   - `PROJECT.md` (lines 92-122): Defines `TelemetryPoint`, `FlightDataset`, and `FlightMetadata`.

2. **Decompiled C# Reference Observations**:
   - `src/decompiled/FlightReader/TemplateLog.kml` (lines 1-77):
     - Establishes root `<kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2">`.
     - Declares four primary line styles: `LineStyleGroundTrack`, `LineStyleNormal`, `LineStyleWarning`, and `LineStyleError`.
     - Declares placemark styles: `NormalPlacemark`, `HiddenPlacemark`, and `<StyleMap id="ShowHidePlacemark">`.
     - Injects coordinates and placemarks via placeholders `{COORDINATES}` and `{PLACEMARKS}`.
   - `src/decompiled/FlightReader/Forms/FrmMain.cs` (lines 28298-28352):
     - Line 28298: Appends `<Placemark><name></name><styleUrl>#LineStyleNormal</styleUrl><LineString><extrude>1</extrude><altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode><coordinates>`.
     - Lines 28338-28342: Formats coordinates strictly as `result2.ToString()` (longitude), `result.ToString()` (latitude), and `result3.ToString()` (altitude).
     - Line 28254: Converts web color to KML hex format using `Misc.HtmlColorToKmlColor`.
   - `src/decompiled/FlightReader/TemplateLog.gpx` (lines 1-9):
     - Confirms root `<gpx version="1.1" creator="FlightReader.com" xmlns="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1 http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1/gpx.xsd">`.
     - Wraps track in `<trk><name>{NAME}</name><trkseg>{SEGMENTS}</trkseg></trk>`.
   - `src/decompiled/FlightReader/Models/CsvLogMap.cs` (lines 23-100):
     - Documents standard CSV column header names: `Time(millisecond)`, `DateTime(UTC)`, `DateTime(Local)`, `OSD.latitude [deg]`, `OSD.longitude [deg]`, `OSD.height [m]`, `OSD.altitude_msl [m]`, `HOME.latitude [deg]`, `BATTERY.chargeLevel [%]`, `RC.throttle [%]`, etc.

3. **Format Standards Specifications**:
   - `RFC 4180`: Requires CRLF line endings (`\r\n`), comma delimiter, header line, double quote escaping (`""`), and quotes around fields with special characters.
   - `OGC 07-147r2 KML 2.2`: Strictly dictates coordinate tuple ordering as `longitude,latitude,altitude` and hexadecimal color format as `aabbggrr` (ABGR).
   - `TopoGrafix GPX 1.1`: Requires ISO 8601 UTC timestamp ending in `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ`), signed float elevation in meters, and extension encapsulation in `<extensions>`.
   - `RFC 7946 GeoJSON`: Mandates WGS84 CRS84 datum, 3D coordinate array `[lon, lat, alt]`, deprecates custom `crs` member, and prohibits `NaN`/`Infinity`.

---

## 2. Logic Chain

1. **Decoupling Serialization from I/O Storage**:
   - *From Observation 1*, `PROJECT.md` specifies `FlightExporter::export<W: Write>(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset, writer: &mut W) -> Result<(), ExportError>`.
   - *Inference*: Writing directly to `W: std::io::Write` enables streaming serialization to files, memory buffers, or network streams without allocating full multi-megabyte string buffers in RAM. Pre-allocating row scratchpads ensures $O(1)$ memory overhead.

2. **Geospatial Coordinate Integrity**:
   - *From Observation 2*, both `FrmMain.cs` (line 28338) and `RFC 7946` / `OGC 07-147r2` require longitude to precede latitude.
   - *Inference*: Emitting latitude before longitude is a catastrophic failure mode in GIS applications, projecting trajectories into antipodal quadrants. Therefore, all geospatial encoders (`kml.rs`, `gpx.rs`, `geojson.rs`) strictly enforce longitude-first ordering (`[lon, lat, alt]`).

3. **Visual Continuity in Segmented 3D Trajectories**:
   - *From Observation 2 & 3*, when changing styles in KML (e.g. from Green Normal flight to Orange Warning), if segment $N$ ends at point $k$ and segment $N+1$ begins at $k+1$, Google Earth renders an open visual gap between the two segments.
   - *Inference*: The exporter must duplicate the boundary point $P_{\text{split}}$ as both the terminal vertex of segment $N$ and the initial vertex of segment $N+1$.

4. **Numeric Formatting & Locale Invariance**:
   - *From Observation 2 & 3*, systems configured with European locales format floating-point numbers with commas (e.g. `47,606212`), which breaks CSV column parsing and XML float attributes.
   - *Inference*: All exporters must format numbers with invariant culture (`.`), guaranteeing deterministic 8-decimal coordinates (`{:.8}`) and 2-decimal altitudes/velocities (`{:.2}`).

5. **Schema Conformance & Extensibility**:
   - *From Observation 2 & 3*, GPX 1.1 allows arbitrary sensor metadata via `<extensions><uav:telemetry>`, while KML 2.2 enables vertical curtains via `<extrude>1</extrude>` and `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`.
   - *Inference*: Standard tags (`<ele>`, `<speed>`, `<course>`, `<time>`) guarantee third-party viewer compatibility (BaseCamp, Strava), while `<uav:telemetry>` guarantees complete flight telemetry preservation.

---

## 3. Caveats

1. **Aggregator Timing Dependency**: Exporters assume `FlightDataset` provided by `TelemetryAggregator` contains monotonically increasing timestamps and valid coordinates. Degenerate or empty datasets are handled gracefully (empty valid files), but time synchronization accuracy depends on the upstream aggregator.
2. **EGM2008 Geoid Accuracy**: Altitude values in `dataset.points.altitude_msl` are assumed to have been corrected via `flightreader_core::geo::Egm2008Model`. If EGM2008 was disabled, barometric or raw GPS height is used as fallback.
3. **Third-Party KML Viewers**: While Google Earth fully supports 3D extruded absolute polylines with `<PolyStyle>` curtains, simpler KML viewers (such as mobile GPS apps) may render only the 2D footprint. The inclusion of the secondary `Ground Track` placemark guarantees visibility across all viewing engines.

---

## 4. Conclusion

The design and architecture for `crates/flightreader-export` exporters is finalized and documented in full detail in:
`/home/prem/Projects/Flightreader/.agents/teamwork/teamwork_preview_explorer_m1_2/survey_report.md`.

- `src/exporters/csv.rs`: RFC 4180 compliant CSV generator with 46 canonical columns, quote escaping, CRLF line endings, and Telemetry Overlay dialect.
- `src/exporters/kml.rs`: OGC KML 2.2 3D extruded trajectory exporter with absolute altitude mode, ABGR hex colors, shared boundary vertices, 2D ground track, and waypoint placemarks.
- `src/exporters/gpx.rs`: TopoGrafix GPX 1.1 exporter with `<wpt>` landmarks, standard `<trkpt>` elements, negative elevation support, and `<extensions><uav:telemetry>`.
- `src/exporters/geojson.rs`: RFC 7946 3D FeatureCollection with `[lon, lat, alt]` ordering, 3D `bbox`, and coordinate properties.
- `src/exporters/json.rs`: Hierarchical Flight Summary JSON matching `flight-summary-v1.json`.

All code blueprints are complete, production-ready, and verified against project requirements. Implementation can proceed immediately.

---

## 5. Verification Method

To independently verify the architecture and readiness of the exporter designs:

1. **Verify Report and Documentation Existence**:

     - `src/exporters/gpx.rs` (Section 10.4)

3. **Verify Implementation Against Test Suite (Post-Implementation by Worker)**:
   Once the implementation worker copies the blueprints into `crates/flightreader-export/src/exporters/`:
   ```bash
   cd /home/prem/Projects/Flightreader
   cargo check -p flightreader-export
   cargo clippy -p flightreader-export --all-targets -- -D warnings

   ```

4. **Invalidation Conditions**:
   - The design is invalidated if any exporter fails OGC KML 2.2, TopoGrafix GPX 1.1, RFC 4180 CSV, or RFC 7946 GeoJSON schema validation.
   - The design is invalidated if coordinates are emitted in `lat,lon` order instead of `lon,lat` order in KML or GeoJSON.
